title: Santa Clarita Community College District
orgAddress: 26455 Rockwell Canyon Road, Santa Clarita, CA 91355
orgAliases: Santa Clarita Valley Junior College District (1967)
body:
The Santa Clarita Community College District is the public body that runs College of the Canyons, the valley's community college. Its main campus is in Valencia, at 26455 Rockwell Canyon Road, and a second campus, on 70 acres at 17200 Sierra Highway in Canyon Country, opened for classes on August 27, 2007.[1][2][3] The district lies wholly within Los Angeles County and serves an area of 367 square miles.[2] A board of five trustees elected by the voters governs it. Since 2016 each trustee has been elected by the voters of one of five trustee areas of roughly equal population, and must live in that area; elections fall in November of even-numbered years.[4][17]

Valley voters approved a junior college district on November 21, 1967, and elected its first board the same day: William G. Bonelli Jr., Bruce Fortine, Sheila Dyer, Peter Huntsinger and Edward Muhl.[5] The board began to meet in December.[6] On the evening of Wednesday, December 13, it named the district the Santa Clarita Valley Junior College District, over objections, at a time when the valley itself had no official name.[7] The trustees named the college College of the Canyons on May 15, 1969.[8] "Valley" was later dropped from the district's name, and it took its present name in 1972, when California's junior colleges became community colleges.[9]

The college opened in the fall of 1969 with about 800 students, in the evenings, at Hart High School in Newhall, under Dr. Robert C. Rockwell, the district's first superintendent-president.[10] Voters approved a $4 million building bond in January 1970; the district bought 153.4 acres in Valencia, and the first classes there met in portable buildings on October 5, 1970.[11][12] A second bond, of $8 million, passed on February 6, 1973, and Governor Ronald Reagan dedicated the first permanent building, the Instructional Resource Center named for Bonelli, on April 22, 1974.[12] Bonelli had died in office in February 1972, and his seat was filled at a special election that June.[13] Dr. Dianne G. Van Hook became superintendent-president on July 1, 1988, and the college's later histories call her chancellor.[18]

For most of its history the trustees held numbered seats and were elected at large by every voter in the district, in odd-numbered years.[14][19] In 2015, to settle a lawsuit under the California Voting Rights Act brought by Jim Soliz and Rosemarie Sanchez-Fraser, who argued that at-large voting was a barrier to Latino participation, the board agreed to elect its trustees by area.[15] It adopted five trustee areas on November 4, 2015, and sent them to the Board of Governors of the California Community Colleges for approval in January 2016.[16] The same change moved the district's elections to even-numbered years, and the first election by area was held on November 8, 2016.[14][17]
footnotes: College of the Canyons, "Celebrating 30 Years: 1969-1999" (2000), back cover: "College of the Canyons, Santa Clarita Community College District, 26455 Rockwell Canyon Road, Santa Clarita, CA 91355," as carried on SCVHistory.com, /scvhistory/coc-30thanniversary.htm.

Santa Clarita Community College District, "2016-2022 Educational and Facilities Master Plan," chapter 1: "The District, which sits completely within Los Angeles County, serves a geographic area of 367 square miles"; the Canyon Country Campus is "situated on a 70-acre hillside high-desert property at 17200 Sierra Highway, 9.8 miles east of the District's Valencia Campus," as carried on SCVHistory.com, /scvhistory/cocedmasterplan20162022.htm.

College of the Canyons, "45 Years of Excellence and Innovation: The History of College of the Canyons, 1969-2014" (2015), year by year, 2007: "Located on a 70-acre site along Sierra Highway, the Canyon Country campus opened for classes on Aug. 27," as carried on SCVHistory.com, /scvhistory/coc45years.htm.

Santa Clarita Community College District, "Elections," canyons.edu/administration/board/elections/, as of October 5, 2026: "The Santa Clarita Community College District, which operates College of the Canyons, is governed by a five-member Board of Trustees that is elected by the community. Elections are held bi-annually in even-number years in November"; "The district is divided into five trustee areas, with each trustee representing an area of roughly equal population"; "Trustees are required to reside in the trustee area they are elected to represent."

College of the Canyons, "45 Years of Excellence and Innovation" (2015), pp. 2-4: "On Nov. 21, 1967, they voted overwhelmingly to transform the idea into reality. While they were at it, they also elected a five-member board of trustees"; year by year, 1968-69: "Elected were Dr. William G. Bonelli Jr., Bruce Fortine ..., Sheila Dyer, Peter Huntsinger and Edward Muhl," as carried on SCVHistory.com, /scvhistory/coc45years.htm.
John Green, "Early History of College of the Canyons," College of the Canyons, canyons.edu/about/history.php, as of October 5, 2026: the board "began functioning as an official body on Dec. 5, 1967."

Lionel Rolfe, "Votes for Santa Clarita Valley Junior College District Name," The Newhall Signal and Saugus Enterprise, December 15, 1967: "Valencia Valley's new junior college district was officially named the Santa Clarita Valley Junior College district Wednesday night"; "the significance of the board's decision, of course, is the fact that this valley basin has no official name as yet," as carried on SCVHistory.com, /scvhistory/sg19671215coc.htm.

"'College of the Canyons': The Junior College Is Finally Named," The Newhall Signal and Saugus Enterprise, May 19, 1969: "Valencia Valley's junior college district trustees named their not yet existing college campus College of the Canyons Thursday night," as carried on SCVHistory.com, /scvhistory/sg19671215coc.htm.

College of the Canyons, "45 Years of Excellence and Innovation" (2015), p. 13: "The name of the district was shortened slightly, with the removal of 'Valley' from the Santa Clarita Valley Junior College District. (In fact, the official district name would metamorphose once again when California decided to rename its junior colleges 'community colleges.' The Santa Clarita Community College District became the district's official name in 1972.)," as carried on SCVHistory.com, /scvhistory/coc45years.htm.

Tom Newton, "The First College Ever Opens in Valencia Valley," The Signal, October 3, 1969: "Valley's first and only college is alive and operating with some 800 students, five days a week, from 4 p.m. to 10 p.m., in Newhall"; it "opened its doors and classes began Monday"; "The new college is located at the Hart High School Newhall Avenue campus"; "Dr. Robert C. Rockwell, Superintendent-President of the Junior College District," as carried on SCVHistory.com, /scvhistory/sg19691003coc.htm.

John Green, "Early History of College of the Canyons," canyons.edu/about/history.php: "College of the Canyons officially opened on Sept. 22, 1969"; voters approved "a $4 million construction-bond issue"; the district "purchased 153.4 acres of land"; "The college's first on-campus classes began on Oct. 5, 1970."

College of the Canyons, "45 Years of Excellence and Innovation" (2015), year by year: "JAN. 20, 1970: Seventy-five percent of voters vote 'yes' for a $4 million construction bond"; "On Feb. 6, 1973, local voters exceeded the required" margin for the $8 million bond; "The IRC was officially dedicated by Gov. Ronald Reagan on April 22, 1974," as carried on SCVHistory.com, /scvhistory/coc45years.htm.

"Claffey Elected to COC Board," The Signal, June 23, 1972: "The election was held to fill the vacancy left by the death of Dr. William G. Bonelli, a founding member of the board," as carried on SCVHistory.com, /scvhistory/sg19720614claffey.htm.

"COC Board to Consider Alternative Voting Area Maps," SCVNews.com, October 7, 2015: "At present, the five trustees hold numbered seats but are elected at-large by all voters in the Santa Clarita Valley"; "In addition to implementing by-trustee areas, the district eliminated the numbered-seat trustee election system and moved its elections from odd-numbered years to even-numbered years"; "The trustee elections that are scheduled for November 2015 have been moved to November 2016."

Enzo Marino, "COC Board to Divide Trustee Seats Into Voting Districts," Hometownstation.com, as carried on SCVNews.com, September 23, 2015: the change is "part of a proposed settlement of a lawsuit brought against the college district by local activists Jim Soliz and Rosemarie Sanchez-Fraser, who allege the current at-large voting system is a barrier to Latino participation"; "With a total district population of 267,152 people according to the 2010 U.S. census."

Board of Governors of the California Community Colleges, "Request to Change Election System at Santa Clarita Community College District," agenda item 2.3, January 19-20, 2016: "On November 4, 2015, the Board of Trustees of the Santa Clarita Community College District adopted Resolution No. 2015/2016-10, 'A Resolution of the Board of Trustees of the Santa Clarita Community College District to Adopt Trustee Areas ...'"
SCVHistory.com, "General Election Results, Nov. 8, 2016 (Certified): State, Local": "SANTA CLARITA COMM. COLLEGE (COC) ... Trustee Area 2 ... Trustee Area 4," /scvhistory/citycouncilresults2016.htm.

College of the Canyons, "Dr. Dianne G. Van Hook: 25 Years at the Helm of COC," July 1, 2013: she "arrived for her first day on the job on July 1, 1988" as "superintendent-president," as carried on SCVHistory.com, /scvhistory/dvh070113.htm; College of the Canyons, "45 Years of Excellence and Innovation" (2015), opens with "A Message from the Chancellor," Dr. Dianne G. Van Hook.
County of Los Angeles, Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk, "Final List, Cancelled Elections," November 5, 2013: "Santa Clarita Community College (Seat # 1, 3 and 5 U/T ending 12/03/2015)."

editorNotes.heading: Dates that disagree
editorNotes.note: The college's own history gives its opening day as September 22, 1969; The Signal of Friday, October 3, 1969 says classes "began Monday," which was September 29. The 45th-anniversary book's year-by-year page dates the naming of the district to December 15, 1967, and the naming of the college to May 21, 1968; The Signal, writing at the time, puts the first on Wednesday, December 13, 1967, and the second on Thursday, May 15, 1969, which the book's own narrative also gives. The district's board history lists John Hackney on the board in 1968; the college's histories say he replaced Sheila Dyer in 1969.

editorNotes.heading: Appointed or elected
editorNotes.note: The college's histories say Francis T. Claffey was appointed to Bonelli's seat in 1972. The Signal of June 23, 1972 reports that he won a special election, held because "State law now requires that vacancies be filled by election, not appointment."

editorNotes.heading: Name
editorNotes.note: In 1967 and 1969 The Signal called the valley "Valencia Valley," its editor's name for it, which did not last.

relatedExisting: William S. Hart Union High School District (#21588): the college opened in 1969 in temporary quarters at Hart High School, and the two districts serve the same valley
Hart High School (#16052): the college's first home, 1969-1970
Newhall Land and Farming Company (#15691): sold the district its Valencia campus land and gave the new college $140,000 (45th-anniversary book, p. 7)
Santa Clarita Valley Historical Society (#15493): joint 2007 video with the college's Canyon Country Campus Advisory Committee (/scvhistory/scvhs-coc-cchistory.htm)
Scott Thomas Wilk Sr. (#335): trustee; record says appointed August 23, 2006, elected 2007 and 2011; holds the only link to the role 'College Trustee' (#18329)
Carl Boyer (#15808): trustee; record says 1973 to 1981; the district's board history lists him from 1974-1975 to 1980-1981

Adrian Adams (#28667, body empty): Leon Worden's caption to AA7401 calls 'Trustee Adrian Adams' a COC trustee in April 1974; he is not in the district's board history for 1974-1975, which lists four names. Same man as the Hart trustee record? Not settled
Sheldon Wigdor (#28370, body empty): a Sheldon S. Wigdor stood for Seat 5 in 2003 (CEDA); same person not settled
Teresa Todd (#25427, body empty): a Theresa Todd stood for Seat 3 in 2005 (CEDA); same person not settled

Candidacies for Andrew Taban (#25945, #28841, Hart district): an Andrew 'Andy' Taban stood for Trustee Area 3 in 2024 (CEDA)
Candidacies for Sharlene Duzick / Sharlene Rose Duzick (#25725, #25755, Saugus Union): Sharlene Rose Johnson won Trustee Area 4 in 2024 (CEDA); same person not settled
Photograph #4863, Program Book: Dedication of Permanent COC Campus, 10-26-1970; article #12232 'City, COC: Big steps in right direction'
openQuestions: One record or two: proposed one. The district is one district with one college (two campuses); the district 'operates College of the Canyons' (its elections page) and there is no second college. The college's photographs, yearbooks and history can attach to this record. Title it 'Santa Clarita Community College District' with 'College of the Canyons' and 'COC' as aliases (proposed), or the reverse?
schoolLevel: proposed 'district', so that /civic lists it with the school districts; 'college' would describe what it runs. Your call.

Founding date: proposed the vote, November 21, 1967. The board first met in December 1967 (December 5 per the college; The Signal of December 15 calls the district 'now one-week-old'). The County's or the State's formal order creating the district was not found.

Boundaries: not settled. The master plan gives 367 square miles wholly in Los Angeles County and calls the Hart district 'the only secondary district in our service area'; no source read says which communities are in it (Castaic, Agua Dulce, Acton, Val Verde, Gorman?) or whether its line is the Hart district's. Needs the County's district boundary map or the Chancellor's Office district list.

Elections: 1973 to 1993, 1999, 2007 and 2018 Area 1 are not in any file held; 2022's appointees in lieu are not named. Worth fetching the County's 2018 and 2022 lists of candidates not on the ballot before election records are made.

People: the district's board history names about 40 trustees since 1967. Who earns a person record is your call under PROFILES.md; the archive already has Wilk and Boyer, and Fortine (on the board 1967 to 2016 in the board history), Jenkins (died February 6, 2023, per the board history) and Van Hook have legacy pages (dvh070113, dvh1113, lw2428 for Steven D. Zimmer).

electionGaps: 1967 formation: no vote count found (archive pages, the anniversary books, the college's history page).
1973 to 1993: no contest results found; the district's board history gives the yearly board, which shows who served, not who stood.
1999, 2007: no college rows in CEDA for these years, and the archive holds no County list for them. Scott Wilk's record (#335) says he won election in 2007.
2015 and 2017: no college election. The board moved the November 2015 trustee elections to November 2016 and those of November 2017 to November 2018 (SCVNews.com, October 7, 2015).

2018, Trustee Area 1: CEDA has only Area 5 for 2018, and the archive holds no 2018 County cancelled list. Michael Berger's term ran to November 2018 (SCVNews.com, October 7, 2015) and he is on the board in 2019 (district board history).
2022: Areas 1 and 5 cancelled; appointees not named in any file held.

The County precinct and canvass PDFs in inventory/elections (10880, 2014ElectionResultsbyPreci-5, 2016StatementofVotesCast-4, Final-Certficate-of-Canvas-1, Final-Election-Canvass-Res-2, LACountyFinalVoteCount-3, historical-results-7, LOCAL-APPT-LIST, resolutionNo129-6) carry only City of Santa Clarita contests; none has a college contest. inventory/elections/ceda-scv.json has no college rows (its parser takes only the City and the five school districts); the rows above were read from the same pinned CEDA files.
